finding_dispositions.summary: Replace stale Safari 26 current target with Safari 27.0 on macOS 26 and macOS 15. Keep Safari 26 as historical; absence of a MIME announcement is not support evidence.

Recommend a strict 300000 ms encoded-file ceiling and fail-closed refusal when final duration is over-limit or unverifiable, with local trim/re-encode only after approval and validation. This remains an owner decision because refusal can lose an overrun recording.
Add exploratory separate Ogg Opus and Vorbis candidate strings for full current Safari runtime testing. Safari 18.4's OS-qualified release note does not provide exact audio-only MIME strings.
Add C02 bound to WebKit's Safari 14.1 MediaRecorder history.
Expand S11 with destination-node/two-channel diagnosis, owner advice, reporter closure, and a separate 2026 follow-up that did not confirm the suggested fix; keep it library-specific.

conflicting_records: Critic C01 records Safari 27 release on 2026-09-17
source_conflicts_and_adjudication.resolution: Direct official WebKit page review confirms Safari 27.0 availability on macOS 26 and macOS 15. Use it as the current proposed lane. The page's lack of a MediaRecorder MIME change does not prove support or regression.

conflicting_records: Brief says one memo up to five minutes
Investigator leaves strict encoded limit open
Critic F2 asks for accepted boundary and over-limit result
source_conflicts_and_adjudication.resolution: Recommend a strict 300000 ms final-file ceiling; if over-limit or unmeasurable, refuse export and discard on reset unless a tested local trim path is approved. This is a proposed owner-facing contract, not a product decision already made by the user.

A no-options recorder could be mistaken for a specific MIME fallback
source_conflicts_and_adjudication.resolution: The fixed W3C draft says an empty MIME type leaves container/codec selection to the UA and the actual MIME is set when recording starts. Treat this as a distinct browser-default candidate, then still verify exact actual type and complete output path.

open_uncertainties: Exact PCM audio-only MIME spelling and supported container/codec combinations on any specific current browser build.
The exact Chrome 155 and Safari 27 MIME matrix for each OS/build and proprietary codec configuration.
Whether a recording type also plays in the same browser and whether the downloaded file opens as labeled.
Whether Safari 27 continues the historical Ogg capability on current macOS 15/26 builds.
Hidden-page stop latency and behavior under a frozen or suspended page.
A per-format duration verifier and any trim/re-encode implementation capable of enforcing a strict 300000 ms output ceiling.
Owner acceptance of failure/discard behavior, 64 MiB output cap, hidden-page policy, partial retention, format order, and optional Worklet cost.
Owner selection of temporary mute handling: pause, finalize, or continue with a visible input-interrupted warning.

sources.title: MediaStream Recording
sources.locator: §2.1-2.3 (constructor, MIME, events, start/stop/timeslice), §2.3 isTypeSupported, §6.1 resource exhaustion
sources.observed_operation: Opened the fixed dated report and inspected algorithm text and surrounding context.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: isTypeSupported=true signals format capability only and can still fail for resource reasons; unsupported constructor MIME throws NotSupportedError; the actual current MIME is exposed after start; timeslice events are queued after a UA minimum; all-track-ended stops recording; individual blobs need not be playable while the completed concatenation must be.
sources.applicability: Primary current working-draft API semantics for MediaRecorder lifecycle, negotiation, buffering, and assembly; not a browser/version support matrix.

reviser_independent_rechecks.observed_operation: Opened the fixed W3C report directly and reviewed the cited recorder sections.
reviser_independent_rechecks.result_and_limit: Rechecked the current dated report as governing API evidence; no browser support guarantee.

reviser_independent_rechecks.observed_operation: Inspected the start/timeslice, final event, playable-combination and resource-exhaustion passages.
reviser_independent_rechecks.result_and_limit: Timeslice uses the greater of the requested interval and a UA minimum; events are task-queued; final dataavailable precedes stop; chunks need not individually play but the completed combination must.

reviser_independent_rechecks.observed_operation: Inspected constructor, mimeType attribute, recording-start selection, isTypeSupported empty-string behavior, error and event context in the fixed W3C report.
reviser_independent_rechecks.result_and_limit: An empty MIME value leaves container/codec choice to the UA; the actual recording MIME is filled when recording starts. isTypeSupported with empty string represents UA choice and does not prove a named format or successful capture/export.

sources.title: Media Capture and Streams
sources.locator: §4.3.1.2 track life-cycle and mute/unmute/ended behavior; §8 event summary; §9.1 Navigator Interface Extensions and §9.2 MediaDevices secure-context IDL; §10.1 MediaDevices getUserMedia; §13 permissions integration
sources.observed_operation: Opened fixed dated report; inspected secure-context IDL, permission rejection, track-end and devicechange algorithms.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Microphone-source end reasons beyond application stop are implementation-defined; external ending queues an ended event, while explicit track.stop() does not; permission failure rejects NotAllowedError; a muted or disabled track may yield silence; devicechange is an event on available-device-set changes and can be coalesced.
sources.applicability: Primary stream/permission lifecycle authority; use for app behavior and test design, with browser/OS observations still required.

sources.title: Web Audio API 1.1
sources.locator: §1.32 AudioWorklet; §2.6 rendering an audio graph and render quantum
sources.observed_operation: Opened fixed dated report; inspected worklet scope, rendering-thread operation, configurable quantum, and real-time callback budget context.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: AudioWorkletProcessor runs in an audio rendering scope/thread; default render quantum is 128 frames but render size is configurable; work must meet real-time callback deadlines. The API supplies audio frames, not a finished encoded file/container.
sources.applicability: Primary design input for the custom processing alternative; exact browser worklet behavior and encoder/mux support remain test items.

sources.title: High Resolution Time
sources.observed_operation: Opened the fixed dated report and inspected monotonic-clock and background-throttling conditions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Performance.now values with the same time origin use a monotonic clock and do not decrease with system-clock changes; in backgrounded tabs the user agent may throttle timers and periodic callbacks or freeze them entirely, without affecting monotonic-clock accuracy.
sources.applicability: Primary timekeeping basis for elapsed active-time accounting; proves a reliable clock source, not that a scheduled stop callback runs at its deadline.

reviser_independent_rechecks.observed_operation: Opened the fixed dated W3C report directly.
reviser_independent_rechecks.result_and_limit: Primary timekeeping source; no wall-clock stop guarantee.

reviser_independent_rechecks.observed_operation: Inspected the monotonic clock and background timer passage.
reviser_independent_rechecks.result_and_limit: performance.now is monotonic within its time origin; the user agent may throttle or freeze background timers/callbacks without making the clock inaccurate.

sources.title: HTML Standard — Page visibility
sources.released_version_or_commit: HTML Living Standard, last updated 2026-10-09; mutable living document
sources.locator: §6.2 Page visibility: system visibility state update and visibilitychange event steps
sources.observed_operation: Opened the Page Visibility section of the current Living Standard and read the state, queued task, and event sequence.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The user agent determines system visibility; on change it queues a global task to update document visibility, then fires visibilitychange. Hidden/visible therefore signals a user-agent determination and handler execution is task-queued.
sources.applicability: Supports stop-on-hidden behavior as a signal-driven policy, not an instantaneous or hard real-time guarantee; exact Chrome/Safari behavior must be exercised.
